title: Output trigram logits: an exact (previous token, current token) -> next-token logit table, zero-initialized, added to the readout of the 150-fable bigram-table Lean incumbent (8,955,987 params)
description: Idea: the Engram/n-gram-memory lead continued on the OUTPUT side (no backlog id; nearest are P27/P38 and the 150-fable input bigram), never tried in either protocol: a count-style trigram LM mixed additively into the logits, an exact 11,449 x 107 table read by (prev, cur) at every position in every forward (pretraining, RL fine-tune, sampling), plus the same row on the pretraining-only MTP t+2 logits. The near-deterministic Lean syntax transitions (which token may follow the last two) then cost the trunk nothing at the readout, so ln_f/head and the last blocks model only the genuinely open choices (which premise, which name), which is what expert iteration on length >= 7 proofs has to explore.
hypothesis: 150-fable showed that taking order-2 syntax off the trunk's input helps RL (+14 on 148-fable, with LOWER heldout greedy 0.948 vs 0.9685 and higher train CE, i.e. the gain is not a loss gain). The readout is the other place the trunk pays for syntax: at every proof position the final residual state must be linearly separable into the ~40 syntax-token logits, which pins the last block's representation to token identity rather than proof state. A zero-init (prev, cur) -> next logit table absorbs those transitions in a few hundred AdamW steps (each row is trained only by its own pair, so used rows move fast at lr 1e-3), after which the head's gradient on syntax positions is near zero and the late layers' capacity and Muon steps go to premise choice. Predicted diagnostics if the mechanism works: train/val next-token CE below 150-fable's at the same wall-clock in the first 60 s (bench: val 0.0843 at 60 s), heldout greedy similar or lower, RL round-1 sample_acc similar or higher. Risks: the 1.2M-parameter table is also trained by RL's AdamW and can memorize sampled proofs' surface trigrams; an additive logit table can over-sharpen syntax tokens and cut sample diversity at T=0.8 (would show as fewer new proofs per RL round); and the input bigram already exposes (prev, cur) to block 0, so the marginal gain may be inside seed noise (sd ~44 per seed).
expected_delta: -25 to +30 theorems at >= 7 (central +6) on 150-fable's 673 (665/693/661); pretrain steps ~4,900-5,100 per seed vs 150-fable's 5,060 mean (bench: 12.29 steps/s over the first 60 s and 180 samples/s vs the 13.2 / 186 measured on 148-fable before the bigram table; one gather per token)

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks, hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads and the input bigram embedding table, identical to 150-fable, plus an exact trigram logit table added to the readout
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: Output-side n-gram memory: a (vocab*vocab = 11,449 rows x 107 logits) nn.Embedding `trigram` on the model, indexed by previous_token * vocab + current_token at every position and ADDED TO THE LOGITS: model(idx) = head(ln_f(h)) + trigram[prev*107 + cur] (new ALiBiGPT.readout(x, prev, cur)), in every forward (pretraining, val_loss via the fork's loss_on, RL fine-tune, sampling). `prev` is the same tensor the 150-fable bigram already builds (pad id 0 before position 0; caches[0]['last'] in incremental decoding), so the cached and full forwards see the same pair. Zero-initialized, so the model starts as the exact 150-fable function; trained by the AdamW auxiliary group (lr 1e-3, wd 0.1, same schedule) like the bigram and token embeddings, not by Muon. The pretraining-only MTP t+2 logits get the trigram row of their pair (x_t, x_{t+1}) too. Everything else (blocks, input bigram, MTP module, optimizer, batches, schedule) unchanged
arch.n_params_detail: 150-fable's 7,730,944 + trigram table 11,449 x 107 = 1,225,043 -> 8,955,987 (bench_pretrain.py on an A40: n_params 8,955,987), under the 10M cap. MTP module (pretraining only, not on the model): 922,880 as in 136-fable
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: 150-fable's module tree plus one state_dict key `trigram.weight` (11449, 107); slopes buffer non-persistent as before
arch.kv_cache: unchanged per-block k/v, caches[0]['pos'] and caches[0]['last'] (B, 1); the `prev` tensor that indexes the input bigram also indexes the output trigram row, so no new cache state

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial); the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (256,512) input proj) join the Muon group and its LayerNorm gains/biases and projection biases join AdamW, same lr, schedule and decay as the trunk; the new bigram table is a non-hidden embedding and joins the AdamW auxiliary group (embeddings, LayerNorm gains/biases, projection biases) at lr 1e-3, wd 0.1
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock with CHANGED floor: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak (115-fable: 0.1 x peak). Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 follows the same factor, and so does its per-step decoupled decay lr * MUON_WD

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor CHANGED 0.1 -> 0.3); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm; the new trigram logit table (11,449 x 107) is a non-hidden embedding and joins the AdamW auxiliary group at lr 1e-3, wd 0.1, exactly like 150-fable's bigram table
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 129's 24 hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (256,512; RMS shape scale sqrt(2)): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are unchanged

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, warmup, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged. The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1. The MTP module gets the same fork _init (normal 0.02, zero biases) followed by orthogonal_ on its 2D parameters (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so the (256,512) proj has element std 0.02); its LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0. Trunk RNG draws are identical to 129 up to the MTP module's construction, which happens after the trunk is built. The trigram logit table is zero-initialized (torch.nn.init.zeros_), so logits at step 0 equal 150-fable's

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions, unchanged, but model(idx) now returns head(ln_f(h)) + trigram[prev*107 + cur]; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 150-fable
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions; CHANGED: the t+2 logits are head(ln_f(z)) + trigram[x_t*107 + x_{t+1}], the same table row a main-path prediction of x_{t+2} would use once x_{t+1} is known, so the MTP block is not asked to re-derive the syntax the main path gets from the table
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]
loss.trigram_check: bench_pretrain.py (A40, 60 s of the real pretrain()): 740 steps, 12.29 steps/s, train CE 0.0712, val CE 0.0843, 5.31 GB peak, 4,096 samples at 180 samples/s with sample_acc 0.075, so training, val and cached sampling all run with the new readout
